label: Week 37, 2026
recap:
This was a quiet week for US AI policy, with just two bill movements recorded and no case updates or federal documents. Activity was split evenly between Pennsylvania and the United States Congress, one jurisdiction each, so there was no concentration of action in any single place.

Two themes appeared in the data. Children and minors was represented by United States Congress HB10315, covering areas such as companion chatbots, age verification, and protections for people under eighteen. Infrastructure and energy was represented by Pennsylvania HB2760, touching on data centers and the local costs of hosting them. Both bill movements reflect a change in status for those records, not any final passage or enactment.

reading.body:
No bills moved, no cases advanced, and no federal documents were recorded in US AI policy between September 7 and 13, 2026.

The week produced no measurable activity across any tracked category: legislation, litigation, or federal agency action. This absence could reflect genuine lull, gaps in data collection, or the summer-fall transition typical in policy cycles. Without positive indicators of movement, the record shows only silence.

The lack of activity means nothing can be inferred about regulatory momentum, court precedent, or agency priorities during this period. This data documents what did not happen rather than what did.
